problem: Determine the equation of the tangent plane to the surface $z={x}^{2}-2{y}^{2}+3$ at the point $(0,1,1).$

feedback.problem: Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface $z=\operatorname{arctan}⁡({x}^{2}y)-{y}^{3}$ at the point $(2,0,0).$
feedback.worked_solution:
The Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the surface $z=f(x,y)$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ on the surface can be written as

$$
z-{z}_{0}=(x-{x}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂x}({x}_{0},{y}_{0})+(y-{y}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂y}({x}_{0},{y}_{0}).
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡({x}^{2}y)-{y}^{3}) \\  & =\frac{1}{({x}^{2}y)^{2}+1}\cdot 2xy \\  & =\frac{2xy}{{x}^{4}{y}^{2}+1} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡({x}^{2}y)-{y}^{3}) \\  & =\frac{1}{({x}^{2}y)^{2}+1}\cdot {x}^{2}-3{y}^{2} \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{{x}^{4}{y}^{2}+1}-3{y}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we evaluate the partial derivatives at $(x,y)=(2,0):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}(2,0) & =\frac{2(2)(0)}{(2)^{4}(0)^{2}+1}=0 \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y}(2,0) & =\frac{(2)^{2}}{(2)^{4}(0)^{2}+1}-3(0)^{2}=4\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, we write down the equation of the tangent plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}z-0 & =(x-0)\frac{∂f}{∂x}(2,0)+(y-0)\frac{∂f}{∂y}(2,0) \\ z & =0(x-0)+4(y-0) \\ z & =4y \\ 4y-z & =0\end{aligned}
$$
